# Brenoxalin added to metformin in type 2 diabetes: a 24-week dose-ranging trial

## Abstract

We tested Brenoxalin, an oral once-daily glucose-lowering drug, in adults with type 2 diabetes on metformin.
Patients took Brenoxalin 10 mg, 20 mg or 40 mg, or placebo, for 24 weeks. HbA1c fell with every dose, and the
largest effect was seen with 40 mg.

## 1. Methods

This was a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial run in 2025. In total, 412 patients were randomised
to four arms (n = 103 per arm). The main measure was the change in HbA1c from baseline; body weight and fasting
plasma glucose were also measured at week 12 and week 24. All values are mean differences vs placebo.

## 2. Results

At week 24, Brenoxalin lowered HbA1c by 0.57 percentage points with 10 mg, by 0.78 percentage points with 20 mg
and by 0.91 percentage points with 40 mg, compared with placebo (all P < 0.001). The dose response was flat
above 20 mg.

Table 1: Mean difference vs placebo at week 12 and week 24.

| Dose | Week | HbA1c change (percentage points) | Body weight change (kg) | Fasting plasma glucose change (mmol/L) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 mg | 12 | −0.46 | −0.6 | −0.75 |
| 10 mg | 24 | see text | −0.7 | −0.84 |
| 20 mg | 12 | −0.72 | −0.9 | −0.97 |
| 20 mg | 24 | see text | −1.2 | −0.99 |
| 40 mg | 12 | −0.90 | −1.2 | −1.25 |
| 40 mg | 24 | see text | −1.3 | −1.25 |

Weight fell with every dose. Hypoglycaemia was rare (3 events in total).

## 3. Discussion

Brenoxalin lowered HbA1c and weight at all three doses over 24 weeks.
